solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Model about to be caught by runner, a wild beast

indicators.note: something caught by another is held inside it, so the reversed model goes within the runner

parts.note: Sebastian Coe, the British Olympic middle-distance runner

indicators.note: about signals turning the word for a model round to read backwards

parts.note: a toy is a small model, such as a toy car

explanation.surface: A model is snatched by someone running past, alongside talk of a wild animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the model and 'to be caught by' sets it inside the runner: Sebastian Coe, the British Olympic champion.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an example: the North American prairie wolf is a wild animal of the dog family.

clue.text: Irresponsible embrace in which 'love' is devoid of content

indicators.note: in which means the following letters go inside the embrace

parts.note: a caress is a gentle embrace or stroke

indicators.note: with its contents gone a word keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A hug in which affection has nothing behind it is thoughtless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devoid of content' keeps only the outer letters of love, and 'in which' places them inside the embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: acting heedlessly without due attention is irresponsible behaviour.

clue.text: Boat with children in river capsized

indicators.note: in means the children's letters sit inside the river
capsized means turned over, so in a down entry the word reads upwards

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: A boat carrying children overturns on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' turns TAY into YAT, and CH goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyponym: a sailing or pleasure vessel is a type of boat.

clue.text: Supportive figure, male turning up carrying weight around

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, so the weight holds the reversed letters
around confirms the weight's letters go round the others

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight

indicators.note: turning up in a down entry means reading the word from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A man who supports others, turned up with a heavy load on his back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes MALE into ELAM, which TON holds as T-ELAM-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Architecture: a carved male figure used as a column to hold up a structure is a supporting statue.

clue.text: A writer to entertain this writer — altogether subhuman types?

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
the setter referring to themselves gives me

explanation.surface: An author plays host to the setter, and both are dismissed as less than human.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to entertain' puts ME inside PEN as PE-ME-N; 'this writer' is a crossword convention for the setter, giving ME. 'altogether' simply binds the pieces into one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: primitive hominids imagined between apes and people were dubbed subhuman creatures.

clue.text: US employer using office assistant, lazy type

parts.note: pa is a personal assistant
a drone is an idler who lives off others' work

explanation.surface: An American boss with an office assistant who is idle.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage, especially of immigrants, a boss who hires and controls labourers is an employer.

clue.text: Shabby mother not right to meet a cardinal

indicators.note: not means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: ten is a cardinal number

explanation.surface: A worn-out mother rushes off to meet a church cardinal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it is a cardinal number. 'not right' removes R from MOTHER, giving MOTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something damaged by insects or worn with age looks shabby.

clue.text: Thing unfolded with day's ending?

indicators.note: unfolded means the letters are opened out and rearranged
a word's ending is its last letter

explanation.surface: A garment taken out and unfolded when the day ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfolded' rearranges THING to NIGHT; 'day's ending' adds Y. Read as a whole, it is the garment shaken out at bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is the item unfolded and put on at the close of the day.

clue.text: An ornament or two by phone knocked over

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as in a brace of pheasants

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up upside down, so in a down-reading sense the word is reversed

parts.note: tel is the abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: One or two ornaments end up on the floor because a phone was knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' reverses the phone abbreviation; 'by' just sets it beside the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a band or chain worn round the wrist is a piece of jewellery, an ornament.

clue.text: Right, briefly I'll test loo out — for its essential requirements

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

parts.note: r is the short form of right

explanation.surface: Someone tries out a toilet and checks it has what it needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges R plus the letters of I'LL TEST LOO. 'its' refers back to the loo in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The paper kept beside a lavatory is exactly what a loo cannot do without.

clue.text: Party game's ending with implanted label — another opportunity for childish behaviour?

indicators.note: something implanted is set inside, so the label goes into the middle of the other letters

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a tag is a label tied on something

explanation.surface: A party game ends with labels being stuck on, a chance for adults to act like children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game's ending' gives E; 'with implanted' sets the label between the party and that E. Senility is often called a second childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Old age with senility is called a second childhood, a later chance to behave childishly.

clue.text: Second item to be knocked down in window

parts.note: a lot is an item knocked down by the auctioneer's hammer

explanation.surface: A second object is about to be smashed through a window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked down' suggests demolition, but it is the auction sense: an item sold under the hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A window is a free period in a schedule, the same as a time allocation in a timetable.

clue.text: Accommodation for which no estimate is possible

indicators.note: possible suggests the letters are one possible arrangement of other letters

explanation.surface: Housing so unusual that no one can give a valuation of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is possible' signals a rearrangement of the letters of NO ESTIMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyponym: a flat on two floors with its own entrance is a kind of home, or accommodation.

clue.text: Is in France facing mountains with soldiers — time for isolation

parts.note: est is French for is
a range is a line of mountains
men is a common crossword word for soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: A French scene among mountains and troops, a period of being cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being alienated or separated from others is a state of isolation.

clue.text: Flag's new image nation finally accepted

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a redesign gives something a new look

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A country's flag gets a new design, and the nation finally approves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nation finally' gives N, which 'accepted' puts inside REDESIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the red banner flown by British merchant ships is a national flag.

clue.text: Fellow I give big meal to, though without a show

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: without means the letter is left out

parts.note: a feast is a big meal

explanation.surface: A man is given a banquet, yet no performance follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a' removes A from FEAST, leaving FEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to display or reveal something plainly is to show it.

clue.text: Go away thinking about section of the organisation?

parts.note: to depart is to go away
mental means relating to thinking or the mind

explanation.surface: Someone thinking about leaving one section of a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: something relating to a division of a company, or concerning a section of an organisation.

clue.text: One attached to craft as decorator?

definitions.meaning: a rope at the bow of a boat used for tying it up
someone who paints walls and woodwork

explanation.surface: A craftsman takes on work as a decorator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests a skill, but it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a mooring rope on a small boat and a house decorator.

clue.text: Pot of soup to spoil little child

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A child spoils a pot of soup.
explanation.walkthrough: Marmite is also a British yeast spread, but here it is the French word for a cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: In French cookery the earthenware cooking vessel in which stock or soup is made carries this name.

clue.text: Form of greeting has upset mum unfortunately

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down entry the letters read upwards

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
alas expresses regret, unfortunately

explanation.surface: A greeting has upset mother, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the low bow with the right hand on the forehead is a Muslim greeting.

clue.text: Dad with bad hesitancy in speech must swallow liquid medicine

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the liquid goes into the other letters

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
ill can mean bad, as in ill effects
er is the sound of hesitation in speech
ink is a liquid for writing

explanation.surface: A poorly father, stammering, has to swallow a liquid remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must swallow' places the liquid straight after the father, before the illness and the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyponym: an analgesic drug that relieves pain is a type of medicine.

clue.text: A bit of wood in the hairpiece he removed

indicators.note: removed means these letters are taken away from what is in front

parts.note: a wig is a hairpiece

explanation.surface: A splinter of wood found in the wig a man has taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' takes the he out of the clue's 'the', leaving its first letter before the hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small thin branch is a small piece of wood.

clue.text: Old village in which pagan god would have power

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: An ancient village where a heathen deity would rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic word: a hamlet, surviving in English place names, means an old village.

clue.text: Article penned by tearful Communist

indicators.note: something penned is shut in a pen, so the article goes inside

parts.note: moist eyes are tearful
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece written by a weepy communist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like writing, but it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a follower of Mao Zedong's Chinese doctrine is a type of communist.

clue.text: They go on the snow and jump, given shouts of approval

parts.note: to skip is to jump lightly
ole is the Spanish shout of approval at a bullfight

explanation.surface: Skiers on the snow jump and are cheered.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the sticks a skier carries are planted in the snow at every turn.

clue.text: Folk with jobs largely gone — youngsters needing to be heard

indicators.note: something heard is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: minors are people under the legal age, youngsters

explanation.surface: People whose work has gone have children who need a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's coal pits were almost all closed in the 1980s and 1990s, so most mining jobs disappeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: coal workers in Britain largely lost their livelihoods when the pits closed.

clue.text: Head of State within military establishment could be this

definitions.text: Head of State within military establishment could be this

indicators.note: within means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a depot is a military base or store

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A head of state installed by the army could turn out to be a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of State' gives S, which 'within' puts inside DEPOT; the whole clue also describes a military-backed tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant ruler is a head of state, and one placed by a military base fits a junta.
